reference_sql:
SELECT s.store_code, COUNT(o.order_id) AS n_guest_orders
FROM stores s
LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id AND o.customer_id IS NULL AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-08 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-09 00:00:00'
GROUP BY s.store_code
alternatives: SELECT s.store_code, COUNT(o.order_id) AS n_guest_orders FROM orders o RIGHT JOIN stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id AND o.customer_id IS NULL AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-08 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-09 00:00:00' GROUP BY 1

SELECT s.store_code, COUNT(o.order_id) FILTER (WHERE o.customer_id IS NULL AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-08 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-09 00:00:00') AS n_guest_orders FROM stores s LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id GROUP BY s.store_code

other_way.sql: SELECT s.store_code, COUNT(o.order_id) FILTER (WHERE o.customer_id IS NULL AND o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-03-08 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-03-09 00:00:00') AS n_guest_orders FROM stores s LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.store_id = s.store_id GROUP BY s.store_code
other_way.tradeoff: Counting with FILTER after joining all orders gives the same counts, but it joins far more rows than it keeps.
